title: Controlled Stage D role-scope ownership pilot
purpose: Run the first controlled Stage D multi-agent pilot by adding a deterministic role-scope ownership report and its adversarial contract. The pilot proves that changed paths can be assigned to exactly one developer, contradictory-QA, integrator or governor scope before broader parallel work is considered. It changes no Player runtime, storage behavior, product identity, release artifact, platform domain or accepted first seam.
invariants: Developer, contradictory-QA, integrator and governor write scopes are explicit, machine-checkable and pairwise disjoint.
The implementation pull request changes exactly four Player paths: one developer tool, one QA contract, the mandatory registry and the evidence coverage map.
Only two new files are added under apps/player, keeping the Player working-file budget at or below 150.
No Player runtime source, source manifest, release configuration, artifact, storage owner, key, payload, UI, UX, pedagogy or product identity changes.
The accepted first reversible storage seam remains unchanged.
The new contract is registered exactly once as mandatory and mapped exactly once to the existing source-and-build evidence surface.
No existing mandatory registry entry or evidence-map entry is removed, moved or modified.
The report is deterministic: equivalent inputs produce byte-equivalent JSON after canonical serialization.
Every changed path is normalized and assigned to exactly one role; unowned or multiply-owned paths make the report fail.
Absolute paths, parent traversal and empty paths are rejected.
The tool performs no network access, command execution or repository mutation; it writes only an explicitly requested output file.
The Remote Agent execution uses player-fast; permanent Player CI remains the complete behavioral gate.
Stage D expansion remains blocked until this pilot receives separate governor acceptance.
requiredEvidence: governance-only authorization pull request with Repository governance and PR scope green
post-merge exact current main SHA captured immediately before fresh agent-branch creation
Remote Agent envelope, patch application and player-fast result on one exact branch
mandatory contract report covering positive and adversarial role-scope cases
permanent Player CI, PR scope and repository governance green on the exact tested result
complete changed-path inventory and role-owner assignment
contradictory QA review independent of developer paths
integrator provenance, determinism, evidence-map and rollback review
separate governor acceptance before Stage D expands
adversarialTests: fail when one changed path matches two role scopes by exact pattern
fail when one changed path matches overlapping exact and glob patterns
fail when a changed path has no owner
fail when a role repeats a pattern
fail when a required role scope is missing, empty or not a list
fail on absolute, empty or parent-traversal paths
prove deterministic output when role and changed-path input ordering differs
prove a valid four-role fixture assigns every changed path exactly once
prove CLI returns non-zero on invalid input and zero on valid input
prove no output file is created unless explicitly requested
fail if any existing registry or evidence-map entry changes
fail if any runtime, release, workflow, architecture, platform or held-domain path changes
nonGoals: change release identity or build output
introduce canonical learner or content identifiers
add backend, accounts, synchronization, catalog, commerce, tenancy or marketplace
authorize more than one controlled Stage D pilot
replace canonical PR scope or Remote Agent validation
independentReview: Integrator owns only registry, evidence coverage and durable pilot evidence
Governor owns only the work package, governor state and decisions
Remote Agent Worktree, permanent Player CI, PR scope and repository governance remain independent automated controls
rollback: Revert the pilot implementation merge: remove role_scope_report.py and contract_role_scope.py, restore checks_registry.json and evidence_coverage.json, and retain the governance history. No Player artifact, learner data, storage, identifier or remote-system migration is involved.
